# Ella IMS Documentation

> An IP Multimedia Subsystem for private 4G and 5G networks - easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

An IP Multimedia Subsystem for private 4G and 5G networks - easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

# Home

# Ella IMS

**Ella IMS** lets subscribers of a private 4G or 5G network make voice and video calls. It is an IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) that runs as a single application, designed to be easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

## Key features

- **Voice and video calls** over 4G (VoLTE) and 5G (VoNR).
- **SIM-based authentication** with your existing HSS (IMS-AKA over Cx), and IPsec between phones and the IMS.
- **Voice QoS** from the 4G or 5G core: PCRF over Rx, or PCF over N5 with optional mutual TLS.
- **Application Servers**: connect voicemail, conferencing, supplementary services and other services, routed per subscriber by your HSS (iFCs over ISC).
- **Push-to-talk**: a built-in MCPTT server for group calls with floor control, and an Android client.
- **Call records**: who called whom, when, for how long, and how the call ended.
- **Easy to operate**: a single binary with an embedded database, a web UI, an HTTP API, and Prometheus metrics.

## In this documentation

- [**Tutorials**](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/tutorials/index.md)

# Tutorials

# Tutorials

In this tutorial, we will add voice calls to a private 5G network with Ella IMS.

| Tutorial                                                                                            | Hardware Required                                        | Installation Method | Duration |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------- |
| [Make Your First Voice Call](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/tutorials/first_voice_call/index.md) | An Ella Core 5G network, a second Linux host, two phones | Snap                | ~30 min  |

# Make Your First Voice Call

In this tutorial, we will add Ella IMS to a private 5G network running Ella Core, and make a voice call (VoNR) between two phones.

You can expect to spend about 30 minutes completing this tutorial.

## Pre-requisites

To complete this tutorial, you will need the following:

**Ella Core**

- A 5G network running Ella Core, as built in Ella Core's [Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware)](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/tutorials/getting_started_hardware/) tutorial. In this tutorial, Ella Core's N6 interface, `ens3`, has the address `10.6.0.2`.

**Ella IMS**

- A second Linux machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, on Ella Core's N6 network. In this tutorial, it has the address `10.6.0.5`.

**Phones**

- Two [5G phones that support VoNR](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/supported_mobile_equipment/#phones), each with a SIM provisioned as a subscriber in Ella Core.

## 1. Enable Diameter in Ella Core

On the Ella Core machine, edit the configuration file:

```
sudo vim /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml
```

Under `interfaces`, add the address Ella Core accepts Diameter connections on:

/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml

```
interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.6.0.2"
```

Restart Ella Core:

```
sudo snap restart ella-core.cored
```

## 2. Install Ella IMS

On the Ella IMS machine, install the Ella IMS snap:

```
sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control
```

Edit the configuration file:

```
sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml
```

Set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from:

/var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml

```
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.6.0.5
```

Start Ella IMS:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd
```

## 3. Initialize Ella IMS

Open your browser and navigate to `http://10.6.0.5:5020/`. The **Initialize Ella IMS** page opens.

Enter an email and a password of at least 8 characters, and click **Create**. You should see Ella IMS's **Cores** page.

## 4. Connect Ella IMS to Ella Core

Go to the **Cores** page:

- Under **Peers**, click **Add Peer**, enter `10.6.0.2`, check **HSS** and **PCRF**, and click **Add**.
- Under **HSS**, click the edit icon next to **HSS Realm**, enter `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and click **Update**.
- Under **Voice QoS**, click the edit icon next to **Policy Function**, select **PCRF**, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **PCRF Realm**, enter `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and click **Update**.

Under **Peers**, Ella Core should show as **open**.

## 5. Route the phones' traffic

On the Ella IMS machine, route the phones' voice addresses, which we create in the next step, through Ella Core:

```
sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400
```

## 6. Prepare Ella Core for voice

In the Ella Core UI, go to the **Operator** page and scroll to the **IMS** section. Click the edit icon next to **P-CSCF Addresses**, enter `10.6.0.5`, and click **Update**.

Go to the **Networking** page and open the **Data Networks** tab. Click **Create**, enter `ims` as the **Name**, `10.46.0.0/16` as the **IPv4 Pool**, turn on **IMS (voice and mission critical services)**, and click **Create**.

Go to the **Profiles** page and click on the `default` profile. Click **Add Policy**, enter `voice` as the **Name**, set the **Data Network** to `ims`, and click **Create**.

Go to the **Subscribers** page. For each of the two subscribers, click on it, click the edit icon next to **MSISDN**, enter a number, and click **Update**:

- First subscriber: `+15551230001`
- Second subscriber: `+15551230002`

## 7. Register the phones

On each phone, turn on VoNR, then turn airplane mode on and off.

In Ella IMS, go to the **Registrations** page. You should see both phones.

## 8. Make a call

From the first phone, call `+15551230002`. Answer on the second phone, talk, and hang up.

In Ella IMS, go to the **Calls** page. You should see the call, with the outcome **answered**.

Success

Congratulations! You have made a voice call over your private 5G network, through Ella Core and Ella IMS.

# Enable Push-to-Talk

This guide enables group calls with floor control with Ella IMS's built-in Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) server. The examples use `10.6.0.5` as Ella IMS's SIP address.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella Core**: integrated with Ella IMS, as in [Integrate with Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/integrate_with_ella_core/index.md), and serving as the HSS.
- **Phones**: the Ella MCPTT app, installed as in [Install the Android MCPTT App](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install_android_app/index.md), and a native IMS client that registers with a `reg-id`.
- **SIMs**: with an ISIM you can program.

## 1. Enable the MCPTT server

In `ims.yaml`, set the address phones reach the MCPTT media on, and restart Ella IMS:

```
mcptt:
  media:
    address: 10.6.0.5
```

## 2. Configure Ella Core

In the Ella Core UI:

- **Networking → Data Networks → Create**: `mcx`, with an IP pool and **IMS** on.
- **Profiles → Create**: an MC profile, e.g. `mcptt`. On it, **Add Policy**: a name, data network `mcx`, 5QI/QCI `69`, ARP `3`, **May pre-empt**, **Not pre-emptable**.
- On the MC profile, also add the policies the users had on their previous profile, e.g. `internet` and `ims`.
- **Operator → IMS → Add Application Server**: click **Fill for Ella IMS MCPTT**, then **Add**.
- **Operator → IMS → Add Service Profile**: name `mcptt`; under **Add from preset**, select the **MCPTT** preset and click **Add Criteria**, then click **Add**.
- **Profiles →** the MC profile **→** edit **IMS Service Profiles**: set **MCPTT** to `mcptt`, and **MMTel (voice, SMS)** to the service profile of the users' previous profile, if any, then **Save**.
- **Subscribers**: put each user on the MC profile, with an MSISDN.

## 3. Route the MC traffic

On the Ella IMS host, route the `mcx` IP pool through Ella Core's N6 address, e.g.:

```
sudo ip route add 10.47.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400
```

## 4. Add the users

In the Ella IMS UI, go to **Push-to-Talk → Users**. For each person, click **Add User** and enter:

- **MCPTT ID**: e.g. `alice`.
- **IMS Identities**: the subscriber's MSISDN, e.g. `15550000001`.

## 5. Add a group

Go to **Push-to-Talk → Groups**, click **Add Group**, and enter a group ID, e.g. `fire`, and its members.

## 6. Set up the phones

On each phone:

- Program the SIM's ISIM with `sip:mcptt-<MSISDN>@<home domain>` in a record of EF.IMPU after the first.
- Set the APN to `mcx`.
- In the app's settings, set the user's MCPTT ID as Ella IMS shows it, e.g. `alice@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and groups.

## 7. Make a group call

Start a group call from one phone. The other members' phones should ring, and **Push-to-Talk → Calls** should show the call.

# Enable SMS over IP

This guide lets phones send and receive SMS over IMS with Ella IMS's built-in IP-SM-GW. The examples use `10.3.0.7` as the SMSC's Diameter address and `15550000000` as its service centre address.

## Prerequisites

- **HSS**: an HSS connected to Ella IMS that supports the Sh-Update of SMSRegistrationInfo and forwards routing requests to the IP-SM-GW over S6c.
- **SMSC**: an SMSC with an SGd interface, such as Ella SMSC.
- **MME or SMSF**, for delivery over NAS when IMS fails: reachable over SGd.

## 1. Set the IP-SM-GW number

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **Cores** page. Under **SMS over IP**, click the edit icon next to **IP-SM-GW Number**, enter an E.164 number without `+`, e.g. `15550000100`, and click **Update**.

## 2. Add the SMSC

Under **Peers**, click **Add Peer**, and enter:

- **Address**: `10.3.0.7`.
- **Roles**: **SGd** only.
- **Service Centres**: `15550000000`.
- **Transport**: **SCTP**, for Ella SMSC.
- **Host**: the SMSC's Diameter identity, e.g. `smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org` for Ella SMSC.

Click **Add**.

## 3. Let the HSS reach the IP-SM-GW

Edit the HSS peer, check **Sh** and **S6c**, and click **Update**. If the HSS's core also serves the MME or SMSF, check **SGd** too.

## 4. Add iFCs in the HSS

With Ella Core:

- **Operator → IMS → Add Application Server**: name `ip-sm-gw`, the **IP-SM-GW Name** of the **Cores** page as the **Server Name**, then **Add**.
- **Operator → IMS → Add Service Profile**: name `sms-over-ip`; under **Add from preset**, select the **SMS over IP** preset and the `ip-sm-gw` **Application Server**, click **Add Criteria**, then click **Add**.
- **Profiles →** the subscribers' profile **→** edit **IMS Service Profiles**: set **MMTel (voice, SMS)** to `sms-over-ip`, then **Save**.

With another HSS, add two iFCs to the subscribers' service profiles, with the **IP-SM-GW Name** of the **Cores** page as the server name, e.g. `sip:ipsmgw.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and default handling `SESSION_CONTINUED`:

- A trigger point on method `REGISTER`, with the subscriber's MSISDN as the service information, and **Include Register Request** and **Include Register Response** set.
- A trigger point on method `MESSAGE`, session case `ORIGINATING_REGISTERED`, and header `Content-Type` matching `application/vnd\.3gpp\.sms`.

## 5. Verify

Register a phone with SMS over IP enabled, and send an SMS. `ellaims_ipsmgw_short_messages_total` should count it, with direction `mo` and result `success`.

# Install

Choose one of the installation methods below.

Install the Ella IMS snap:

```
sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control
```

Configure Ella IMS:

```
sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml
```

Start Ella IMS:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd
```

Install the required dependencies:

```
sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc
```

Clone the Ella IMS repository:

```
git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
cd ims
```

Build the frontend:

```
npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui
```

Build Ella IMS:

```
go build -o ims -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/ims/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/ims
```

Configure Ella IMS:

```
vim ims.yaml
```

Start Ella IMS:

```
sudo ./ims --config ims.yaml
```

Create a new directory:

```
mkdir ella-ims
cd ella-ims
```

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml

```
configs:
  ella_ims_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/ims.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5020
      sip:
        addresses: [10.6.0.5]
      diameter:
        address: 10.3.0.5

services:
  ella-ims:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-ims:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_ims_config
        target: /ims.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/ims --config /ims.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    volumes:
      - ella-ims-data:/data

volumes:
  ella-ims-data:
```

Set `sip.addresses` and `diameter.address` to addresses of the host.

Start the Ella IMS container:

```
docker compose up -d
```

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster is running with the [Multus CNI](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multus-cni) installed.

Download the Ella IMS manifests:

```
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
```

Edit `ims/k8s/ims-sip-nad.yaml`: set `master`, the SIP address, and the route to the phones' IP pool through the core's N6 (5G) or SGi (4G) address.

Edit `ims/k8s/ims-diameter-nad.yaml`: set `master` and the Diameter address.

Edit `ims/k8s/ims-configmap.yaml`: set `sip.addresses` and `diameter.address` to the same addresses.

Create the namespace:

```
kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
```

Deploy Ella IMS:

```
kubectl apply -k ims/k8s
```

Ella IMS's UI and API are on the `ella-ims` NodePort Service.

Ella IMS's UI and API are at `http://<host-ip>:5020`. Open the UI and create the first user.

See the [configuration reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/config_file/index.md) for all options.

# Install the Android MCPTT App

This guide installs Ella MCPTT, the push-to-talk app for Ella IMS, on Android phones.

## Prerequisites

- **Phones**: Android 14 or later.
- **SIMs**: access rules (ARA-M) that allow the app's signing certificate, SHA-1 `692EDA27666062D3982DF420E1FEC26FE806335B`.

## 1. Download the app

Download the app and its checksum, and check them:

```
curl -LO https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk
curl -LO https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk.sha256
sha256sum -c ella-mcptt.apk.sha256
```

## 2. Install the app

In your MDM, add `ella-mcptt.apk` as a private or in-house app, and assign it to the phones.

Connect the phone over USB, with USB debugging on, and run:

```
adb install -r ella-mcptt.apk
```

In the phone's browser, open `https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk`, allow the browser to install unknown apps, and install it.

## 3. Grant the permissions

Open Ella MCPTT and go to **Settings → Diagnostics → Permissions**. Tap **Allow** on each item, and allow it in the prompt. It should show **The app has everything it needs.**

To update the app, install a newer APK the same way. Its settings are kept.

# Integrate with an Application Server

This guide connects an Application Server (AS), such as voicemail or conferencing, to Ella IMS. The examples use `10.80.0.30` as the AS's address and `10.6.0.5` as Ella IMS's SIP address.

## Prerequisites

- **HSS**: an HSS that provisions initial Filter Criteria (iFCs).

## 1. Trust the AS

In `ims.yaml`, add the AS's address to the trusted networks, optionally set how long the AS has to answer, and restart Ella IMS:

```
sip:
  trusted_networks: [10.80.0.30/32]
scscf:
  as_timeout: 4s
```

## 2. Add iFCs in the HSS

In the HSS, add iFCs to the subscribers' service profiles, with the AS's SIP URI as the server name, e.g. `sip:10.80.0.30:5060`:

- For third-party registration, add a trigger point on method `REGISTER`. Set **Include Register Request** and **Include Register Response** if the AS needs them.
- For originating or terminating services, add a trigger point on the session case, plus the method, header or Request-URI to match.
- Set the default handling to `SESSION_CONTINUED` to go on without the AS, or to `SESSION_TERMINATED` to fail the call, or deregister the user on `REGISTER`.

## 3. Add the AS's PSIs

If the AS serves its own URIs, such as a conference factory:

- Add its PSIs to the HSS, distinct or wildcarded, with their iFCs or the AS as their server name.
- If the server name is a host name, make it resolve to the AS, with a DNS A or SRV record.

## 4. Configure the AS

On the AS:

- Trust Ella IMS's SIP address, `10.6.0.5`.
- Send requests to a user to the I-CSCF, port `5070`.
- Send requests on behalf of a user or a PSI to the S-CSCF, port `5080`, with `orig` in the Route header, `Route: <sip:10.6.0.5:5080;lr;orig>`, and the user in P-Served-User or P-Asserted-Identity.

## 5. Verify

Register a phone. The AS should receive a third-party REGISTER, or the first request that matches its iFCs.

# Integrate with Ella Core

This guide connects Ella IMS to Ella Core, with Ella Core as the HSS and the PCRF.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella IMS**: installed and started, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md).

The examples use these addresses:

| Address        | Role                                      |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `10.3.0.2`     | Ella Core's Diameter address              |
| `10.6.0.2`     | Ella Core's N6 address                    |
| `10.3.0.5`     | Ella IMS's Diameter address               |
| `10.6.0.5`     | Ella IMS's SIP address                    |
| `10.46.0.0/16` | IP pool of Ella Core's `ims` data network |

## 1. Enable Diameter in Ella Core

In Ella Core's configuration file, set the Diameter address, and restart Ella Core:

```
interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.3.0.2"
```

## 2. Set the Ella IMS addresses

In `ims.yaml`, set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from, and restart Ella IMS:

```
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.5
```

## 3. Set the operator

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **Operator** page:

- Click the edit icon next to **Operator ID (MCC/MNC)**, enter Ella Core's MCC and MNC, e.g. `001` / `01`, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **Numbering Plan**, enter your country code and prefixes, and click **Update**.

## 4. Add Ella Core as the HSS and PCRF

Go to the **Cores** page:

- Under **Peers**, click **Add Peer**, enter `10.3.0.2`, check **HSS** and **PCRF**, and click **Add**.
- Under **HSS**, click the edit icon next to **HSS Realm**, enter `epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`, with the MNC padded to 3 digits, e.g. `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and click **Update**.
- Under **Voice QoS**, click the edit icon next to **Policy Function**, select **PCRF**, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **PCRF Realm**, enter the same realm, and click **Update**.

## 5. Route the phones' traffic

On the Ella IMS host, route the `ims` data network through Ella Core's N6 address:

```
sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400
```

## 6. Point Ella Core to Ella IMS

In Ella Core, set **Operator → IMS → P-CSCF Addresses** to `10.6.0.5`, then follow Ella Core's [Enable Voice](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/enable_voice/) guide.

# Configuration File

Ella IMS is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella IMS with the `--config` flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected.

## Parameters

- `logging` (object, optional): The logging configuration.
  - `level` (string, optional): The log level: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error`. Default `info`.
- `db` (object): The database configuration.
  - `path` (string): The path to the SQLite database file.
- `api` (object): The HTTP API and UI.
  - `address` (string): The IP address to listen on. `0.0.0.0` or `::` for all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
  - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default `5020`.
  - `tls` (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS. Default: plain HTTP.
    - `cert` (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
    - `key` (string): The path to the PEM private key.
- `sip` (object): SIP, for every CSCF.
  - `addresses` (list of strings): The IP addresses the CSCFs listen on and phones reach. At least one; specific addresses, not `0.0.0.0` or `::`.
  - `trusted_networks` (list of strings, optional): The networks, in CIDR notation, of the other nodes of the trust domain, such as Application Servers. The S-CSCF accepts requests only from them, the I-CSCF accepts their asserted identities, and Application Servers are sent requests only in them. Must not cover every address of a family. See [Security](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/security/#the-trust-domain).
- `pcscf` (object, optional): The P-CSCF.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default `5060`.
  - `ipsec` (object, optional): The IPsec ports.
    - `server_port` (int, optional): The protected server port. Default `5063`.
    - `client_ports` (list of 2 ints, optional): The protected client ports. Default `[5064, 5065]`.
- `icscf` (object, optional): The I-CSCF.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default `5070`.
- `scscf` (object, optional): The S-CSCF.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default `5080`.
  - `as_timeout` (duration, optional): How long an Application Server has to respond before the default handling of its iFC applies, e.g. `4s`. Under `32s`. Default `4s`.
- `diameter` (object): Diameter, to the HSS and the PCRF.
  - `address` (string): The IP address of the Diameter connections, advertised to peers. A specific address, not `0.0.0.0` or `::`.
  - `port` (int, optional): The port. Default `3868`.
- `n5` (object, optional): N5, to a PCF. Required to select the PCF as the policy function.
  - `notify` (object): Where the P-CSCF receives the PCF's notifications.
    - `address` (string): The IP address. A specific address, not `0.0.0.0` or `::`.
    - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port. `0`, the default, lets the system choose one. Must differ from the other TCP ports on its address.
  - `tls` (object, optional): Mutual TLS on N5. Required for a PCF URI with the `https` scheme. The files are read when the PCF URI is set.
    - `ca` (string): The path to the PEM file of the CA certificates that the PCF's certificate must chain to.
    - `cert` (string): The path to the PEM file of Ella IMS's certificate, presented as both client and server. Must be valid for `n5.notify.address`.
    - `key` (string): The path to the PEM file of the certificate's private key.
- `mcptt` (object, optional): The built-in MCPTT server. When absent, the MCPTT server doesn't run and opens no ports.
  - `mode` (string, optional): `ims`, the default, or `direct`: the MCPTT server is the registrar of its clients, without the IMS, for labs and tests.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port on each of `sip.addresses`. In `direct` mode, the UDP and TCP port clients send to. Default `5090`.
  - `media` (object): The media relay.
    - `address` (string): The IP address of the media sockets.
    - `advertise` (string, optional): The IP address in the SDP, of the same family as `address`. Required if `address` is `0.0.0.0` or `::`. Default `address`.
    - `min_port` (int, optional): The first port of the voice legs. Even. Default `20000`.
    - `max_port` (int, optional): The last port of the voice legs. Default `20999`.
    - `control_port` (int, optional): The port of the floor control channels, outside the voice legs' range. Default `21000`.

The SIP ports (`pcscf.port`, `pcscf.ipsec.*`, `icscf.port`, `scscf.port`, `mcptt.port`) must all differ, must not be `5100`, which the built-in IP-SM-GW takes, and must differ from `api.port` when the API listens on a SIP address. The IPsec ports cannot be `5060` or `5061`. On a SIP address, the MCPTT media ports must not include a SIP port.

## Example

```
logging:
  level: info
db:
  path: ims.db
api:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 5020
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
pcscf:
  port: 5060
  ipsec:
    server_port: 5063
    client_ports: [5064, 5065]
icscf:
  port: 5070
scscf:
  port: 5080
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.5
  port: 3868
```

# Connectivity

| Interface                      | Peer                                | Transport                          | Address               | Port                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| API                            | Operators, Prometheus               | TCP                                | `api.address`         | `api.port` (`5020`)                                                                                        |
| SIP: P-CSCF                    | Phones                              | UDP and TCP                        | `sip.addresses`       | `pcscf.port` (`5060`)                                                                                      |
| SIP: P-CSCF, IPsec             | Phones                              | UDP and TCP, in ESP                | `sip.addresses`       | `pcscf.ipsec.server_port` (`5063`), `pcscf.ipsec.client_ports` (`5064`, `5065`)                            |
| SIP: I-CSCF                    | Application Servers, other networks | UDP and TCP                        | `sip.addresses`       | `icscf.port` (`5070`)                                                                                      |
| SIP: S-CSCF                    | Application Servers                 | UDP and TCP                        | `sip.addresses`       | `scscf.port` (`5080`)                                                                                      |
| SIP: MCPTT, `direct` mode      | MCPTT clients                       | UDP and TCP                        | `sip.addresses`       | `mcptt.port` (`5090`)                                                                                      |
| MCPTT media                    | MCPTT clients                       | UDP                                | `mcptt.media.address` | `mcptt.media.min_port`–`max_port` (`20000`–`20999`), `mcptt.media.control_port` (`21000`)                  |
| Diameter: Cx, Rx, Sh, S6c, SGd | HSS, PCRF, SMSC, MME, SMSF          | TCP or SCTP, set per peer          | `diameter.address`    | `diameter.port` (`3868`) to receive, over each transport a peer uses; each peer's port (`3868`) to connect |
| N5                             | PCF                                 | HTTP/2, optionally with mutual TLS | `n5.notify.address`   | `n5.notify.port` (chosen by the system), while the policy interface is `n5`                                |

Defaults are in parentheses.

## Requirements

- **ESP**: firewalls between phones and Ella IMS must pass ESP (IP protocol 50).
- **`CAP_NET_ADMIN`**: Ella IMS sets up IPsec in the kernel. Run it as root, connect the snap's `network-control` interface, or add the capability to its container. On Kubernetes, only the `privileged` Pod Security Standard allows it.
- **Routes**: Ella IMS needs a route to the phones' IP pools through the core network's N6 (5G) or SGi (4G) address.

# Metrics

Ella IMS exposes Prometheus metrics at `GET /api/v1/metrics`.

| Metric                                    | Type                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ellaims_build_info`                      | Gauge                   | Always 1. The version and revision of the running build are in its labels.                                                                                                                                       |
| `ellaims_registered_subscribers`          | Gauge                   | Subscribers registered now.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `ellaims_registration_attempts_total`     | Counter                 | Registrations and re-registrations, by result: `accept`, `auth_failure`, `reject`.                                                                                                                               |
| `ellaims_active_calls`                    | Gauge                   | Calls in progress.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `ellaims_calls_total`                     | Counter                 | Calls that ended, by outcome: `answered`, `cancelled`, `busy`, `rejected`, `no_answer`, `unavailable`, `failed`.                                                                                                 |
| `ellaims_sip_responses_total`             | Counter                 | Final responses the P-CSCF sent to phones, by method and status class.                                                                                                                                           |
| `ellaims_diameter_peer_up`                | Gauge                   | 1 if the connection to a Diameter peer is open, by peer and application.                                                                                                                                         |
| `ellaims_peer_requests_total`             | Counter                 | Requests to the HSS, the policy function, the SMSCs and the MMEs and SMSFs, by interface (`cx`, `rx`, `n5`, `sh`, `s6c`, `sgd`) and result (`success`, `failure`, `error`, `timeout`).                           |
| `ellaims_peer_request_duration_seconds`   | Histogram               | Duration of requests to the HSS, the policy function, the SMSCs and the MMEs and SMSFs, by interface.                                                                                                            |
| `ellaims_ipsmgw_short_messages_total`     | Counter                 | Short messages the IP-SM-GW carried, by direction (`mo`, `mt`), domain (`smsc` for `mo`; `ims`, `mme`, `sgsn`, `smsf_3gpp`, `smsf_non_3gpp`, `none` for `mt`, the last tried) and result (`success`, `failure`). |
| `ellaims_database_query_duration_seconds` | Histogram               | Duration of database calls, by connection pool: `write`, `read`.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ellaims_database_query_errors_total`     | Counter                 | Failed database calls, by connection pool.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `ellaims_database_storage_bytes`          | Gauge                   | Size of the database on disk, by file: `main`, `wal`.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `go_*`                                    | Gauge, Counter, Summary | Go runtime: goroutines, heap, garbage-collection pauses.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `process_*`                               | Gauge, Counter          | Process: memory, CPU, open file descriptors, start time.                                                                                                                                                         |

# Performance

Measured registration and call capacity of Ella IMS, with 20,000 registered subscribers on a 4 vCPU host.

## Registrations

Registration time: from the initial REGISTER to its 200 OK, through the IMS-AKA challenge, measured at the phone (TS 32.409 §4.1.1.1).

| Load                                       | Rate (/s) | Initial registration success rate | Mean  | p99    | CPU (cores) |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------- | --------------------------------- | ----- | ------ | ----------- |
| From 0 to 20,000 registered, in 3 min 20 s | 100       | 100%                              | 21 ms | 81 ms  | —           |
| 20,000 registered                          | 50        | 100%                              | 32 ms | 127 ms | 0.58        |
| 20,000 registered                          | 100       | 100%                              | 56 ms | 1.04 s | 1.19        |
| 20,000 registered                          | 150       | 100%                              | 2.6 s | 4.5 s  | 1.43        |

| Re-registration              | Value                                                                      |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rate                         | 6.7/s: each of the 20,000 subscribers every 3,000 s (TS 24.229 §5.1.1.4.1) |
| Re-registration success rate | 100%                                                                       |
| Mean                         | 19 ms                                                                      |
| p99                          | 97 ms                                                                      |

## Calls

Voice calls with preconditions (IR.92 §2.4.1), answered at once and held 90 s. Session setup time: from the INVITE to the first 180 or 2xx, measured at the calling phone (TS 32.409 §4.1.2.6).

| Rate (/s) | Calls per hour | Session establishment success rate | Call drop rate | Session setup time, mean | p99    | Calls in progress | CPU (cores) | Resident memory |
| --------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ | ------ | ----------------- | ----------- | --------------- |
| 25        | 90,000         | 100%                               | 0%             | 42 ms                    | 129 ms | 1,499             | 0.26        | 1.8 GiB         |
| 50        | 180,000        | 100%                               | 0%             | 57 ms                    | 155 ms | 2,999             | 0.47        | 2.0 GiB         |
| 100       | 360,000        | 100%                               | 0%             | 59 ms                    | 150 ms | 6,000             | 0.93        | 2.7 GiB         |

## Memory

| Item                                      | Value                     |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Resident memory, idle                     | 25 MiB                    |
| Resident memory per registered subscriber | 76 KiB                    |
| Memory of ended calls                     | Released within 2 minutes |

## Limits

| Limit                  | Value                                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Registered subscribers | 20,000 tested                                                                                 |
| SIP TCP connections    | 3/4 of the open-file limit: 393,216 at systemd's default of 524,288. Each phone uses up to 2. |
| MCPTT users            | 1,000                                                                                         |

## Host Requirements

| Requirement                   | Value                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Receive Packet Steering (RPS) | On all CPUs, on a network interface with a single receive queue: `/sys/class/net/<interface>/queues/rx-0/rps_cpus`. Without it, one CPU processes all incoming traffic. |
| Linux 6.13 and later          | The kernel's processing of incoming IPsec traffic grows with the number of registered phones per receiving CPU.                                                         |

## Test Setup

| Item             | Value                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Version          | Ella IMS built from source, after v0.0.1, default configuration                                                                                                    |
| Host             | VM, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, Ubuntu 26.04, Linux 7.0, on an Intel Core Ultra 7 265K                                                                                       |
| Network          | One receive queue, RPS on all 4 CPUs                                                                                                                               |
| Open-file limit  | 524,288 (systemd default)                                                                                                                                          |
| Load generator   | Separate VM, 10 vCPU, 10 GB RAM                                                                                                                                    |
| Phones           | Simulated: IMS-AKA, IPsec with integrity protection only (`hmac-sha-1-96`, no encryption), SIP over TCP, one IP address per phone, registration event subscription |
| Re-registrations | Not re-authenticated (S-CSCF default)                                                                                                                              |
| HSS              | Simulated, over Cx: 2.5 ms mean response time                                                                                                                      |
| Policy           | Simulated PCRF, over Rx: 3.6 ms mean response time                                                                                                                 |
| Media            | Not carried by Ella IMS                                                                                                                                            |

# Supported Mobile Equipment

Ella IMS follows 3GPP standards. Any compliant core network, Application Server and phone should work with it. This page lists those validated against Ella IMS.

## Core Networks

- **[Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/)**
- **[Open5GS](https://open5gs.org/)**

## Phones

- **Apple iPhone 11**
- **Apple iPhone 16**
- **Crosscall Core-Z5**
- **Google Pixel 10a**
- **Motorola Moto G 5G**
- **Samsung Galaxy A56**

## MCPTT Clients

- **Ella MCPTT for Android**, in the [`android`](https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/tree/main/android) directory.

## Phone Quirks

| Phone              | RAT | Observed                                                                           |
| ------------------ | --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Apple iPhone 11    | 4G  | Live Voicemail answers declined and unanswered calls (`200 OK`).                   |
| Apple iPhone 16    | 4G  | Live Voicemail answers declined and unanswered calls (`200 OK`).                   |
|                    | 4G  | 3 IMS addresses in 6 minutes.                                                      |
|                    | 4G  | No video calls: registers with `audio` only, no `video` feature tag.               |
|                    | 5G  | 5G SA unavailable without SUCI on the SIM (USIM service 124, `EF.SUCI_Calc_Info`). |
|                    | 5G  | Rejects NEA0 (Security Mode Reject, cause 24).                                     |
|                    | 5G  | SIM PLMN 001/01: never attempts the 5G SA cell.                                    |
|                    | 5G  | SIM PLMN 999/01: data only, no voice settings, no IMS PDU session.                 |
| Google Pixel 10a   | 4G  | Video call to an iPhone: the dialer offers Google Meet instead.                    |
| Motorola Moto G 5G | 5G  | SIM PLMN 999/01: 5G SA only with network type "NR only".                           |
|                    | 5G  | Video call answered without a camera, then switched to `recvonly` (once in 5).     |
|                    | 4G  | SIM PLMN 999/01: IMS doesn't start.                                                |
| Samsung Galaxy A56 | 4G  | SIM PLMN 001/01: VoLTE off (`LABSIM` profile, TS.43 entitlement 403).              |

# System Requirements

Ella IMS runs on Linux. It supports **amd64** and **arm64** architectures.

|                      | Production                                                                                                            |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CPU**              | 4 cores                                                                                                               |
| **Memory**           | 8 GB RAM                                                                                                              |
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS                                                                                                      |
| **Kernel**           | IPsec: `xfrm_user`, `esp4`, `esp6` for IPv6, and `authenc`. SCTP, for Diameter peers over SCTP.                       |
| **Privileges**       | `CAP_NET_ADMIN` (see the [connectivity reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/connectivity/index.md)) |

The production host is the one of the [performance reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/performance/index.md): 20,000 registered subscribers.

# API

## Authentication

Requests send a token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The token is either:

- an access token, from [log in](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/auth/#log-in) or [refresh the access token](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/auth/#refresh-the-access-token), valid for 15 minutes;
- an [API token](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/users/#create-an-api-token), which starts with `ellaims_`.

These paths take no token: `GET /api/v1/livez`, `GET /api/v1/readyz`, `GET /api/v1/status`, `GET /api/v1/metrics`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml`, `POST /api/v1/init`, and `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `/refresh` and `/logout`.

### Roles

| Role            | `role_id` | Allows                                                                         |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Admin           | `1`       | Everything.                                                                    |
| Read Only       | `2`       | Reading the settings, the registrations, the call records and the MCPTT state. |
| Network Manager | `3`       | Read Only, plus changing the settings and re-authenticating registrations.     |

Only an Admin manages users. Every user reads its own user, changes its own password, and manages its own API tokens.

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users.

## Responses

Ella IMS's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a `result`:

```
{
    "result": "Result content"
}
```

A failed response carries an `error`:

```
{
    "error": "Error message"
}
```

`GET /api/v1/livez` and `GET /api/v1/readyz` answer 204 with no body when they succeed. `GET /api/v1/metrics` returns text in the [Prometheus exposition format](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/#text-format-details), `GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml` returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

## OpenAPI Specification

The full API is described by an [OpenAPI 3.1](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0) specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella IMS instance:

```
GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml
```

## Status codes

- 200 - Success.
- 201 - Created.
- 202 - Accepted.
- 204 - No content.
- 400 - Bad request.
- 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
- 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
- 404 - Not found.
- 405 - Method not allowed.
- 409 - Conflict.
- 429 - Too many requests. `Retry-After` is the seconds to wait.
- 500 - Internal server error.
- 503 - Service unavailable, or not ready. See [Check readiness](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/status/#check-readiness).

# Authentication

## Log In

This path returns an access token, and sets the session cookie, `ims_session`, or `__Host-ims_session` over TLS. The session lasts 30 days, and a user has at most 10.

| Method | Path                 |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/login` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description                 |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------- |
| `email`    | string | Yes      | Email address, in any case. |
| `password` | string | Yes      | Password.                   |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` | Wrong email or password.                                                                                                                 |
| `429` | More than 20 attempts in a minute from the client address, or its IPv6 /64; or more than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Login successful",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

## Refresh the Access Token

This path returns a new access token for the session of the cookie.

| Method | Path                   |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/refresh` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                       |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` | No session, or the session ended. The response clears the cookie. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

## Log Out

This path ends the session of the cookie, and its access tokens, and clears the cookie.

| Method | Path                  |
| ------ | --------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/logout` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                |
| ----- | -------------------------- |
| `204` | Logged out, or no session. |

# Call Records

A call record describes a call the IMS handled, after TS 32.298 §5.1.3.1.

## List Call Records

This path returns the list of call records, most recently requested first.

| Method | Path                   |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/call-records` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed                                                                           | Description                                                                  |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `search`   | query | str  |         |                                                                                   | Substring of the ICID or of an identity of the caller or the callee.         |
| `start`    | query | str  |         |                                                                                   | Inclusive lower bound of the request time, RFC 3339. Unbounded when omitted. |
| `end`      | query | str  |         |                                                                                   | Exclusive upper bound of the request time, RFC 3339. Unbounded when omitted. |
| `outcome`  | query | str  |         | `answered`, `cancelled`, `busy`, `rejected`, `no_answer`, `unavailable`, `failed` | Outcome to include. Repeatable.                                              |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`                                                                            | 1-based page index.                                                          |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100`                                                                           | Number of items per page.                                                    |

### Response Fields

| Field               | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | int     | Record identifier.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `icid`              | string  | icid-value of the P-Charging-Vector (§5.1.3.1.19).                                                                                                                                     |
| `session_id`        | string  | Call-ID of the INVITE (§5.1.3.1.59).                                                                                                                                                   |
| `calling_party`     | array   | P-Asserted-Identity values (§5.1.3.1.24).                                                                                                                                              |
| `caller_impi`       | string  | Private user identity of the caller (§5.1.3.1.36).                                                                                                                                     |
| `requested_party`   | string  | Request-URI from the caller (§5.1.3.1.43).                                                                                                                                             |
| `called_party`      | string  | Request-URI after normalisation by the S-CSCF (§5.1.3.1.9).                                                                                                                            |
| `callee_impi`       | string  | Private user identity of the answering registration (§5.1.3.1.36).                                                                                                                     |
| `requested_at`      | string  | Reception time of the INVITE (§5.1.3.1.58).                                                                                                                                            |
| `delivery_start_at` | string  | Time of the final response to the caller (§5.1.3.1.55).                                                                                                                                |
| `delivery_end_at`   | string  | End time of an answered call (§5.1.3.1.54).                                                                                                                                            |
| `sip_status`        | int     | Final status of the INVITE sent to the caller (§5.1.3.1.57).                                                                                                                           |
| `outcome`           | string  | `answered` (2xx), `cancelled` (487 to a caller CANCEL), `busy` (486, 600), `rejected` (603), `no_answer` (408 after a 180), `unavailable` (480), or `failed` (any other final status). |
| `ended_by`          | string  | `caller`, `callee` or `network`.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `alerted`           | boolean | Whether a 180 reached the caller.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `media`             | array   | Media types of the accepted m-lines.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `in_progress`       | boolean | Whether the call has not ended.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `incomplete`        | boolean | Whether the record was closed without the end of the call.                                                                                                                             |
| `duration_ms`       | int     | Duration of an answered call that ended, in milliseconds.                                                                                                                              |

A value the IMS did not observe is absent. Times are RFC 3339.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 42,
                "icid": "1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b",
                "session_id": "a84b4c76e66710@10.45.0.2",
                "calling_party": [
                    "sip:+15550000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                    "tel:+15550000001"
                ],
                "caller_impi": "001010000000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "requested_party": "tel:15550000002",
                "called_party": "tel:+15550000002",
                "callee_impi": "001010000000002@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "requested_at": "2026-10-26T18:21:10.204Z",
                "delivery_start_at": "2026-10-26T18:21:14.871Z",
                "delivery_end_at": "2026-10-26T18:23:02.330Z",
                "sip_status": 200,
                "outcome": "answered",
                "ended_by": "caller",
                "alerted": true,
                "media": ["audio"],
                "in_progress": false,
                "incomplete": false,
                "duration_ms": 107459
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}
```

## Get a Call Record

| ------ | --------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/call-records/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type | Description        |
| ---- | ---- | ------------------ |
| `id` | int  | Record identifier. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                    |
| ----- | ------------------------------ |
| `404` | No record has this identifier. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": 43,
        "icid": "2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c",
        "session_id": "b95c5d87f77821@10.45.0.3",
        "calling_party": [
            "sip:+15550000002@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"
        ],
        "caller_impi": "001010000000002@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "requested_party": "tel:+15550000001",
        "called_party": "tel:+15550000001",
        "requested_at": "2026-10-26T18:30:41.019Z",
        "delivery_start_at": "2026-10-26T18:30:50.552Z",
        "sip_status": 486,
        "outcome": "busy",
        "ended_by": "callee",
        "alerted": true,
        "media": [],
        "in_progress": false,
        "incomplete": false
    }
}
```

## Get Call Record Retention Policy

This path returns how long call records are kept.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/call-records/retention` |

### Response Fields

| Field  | Type | Description                           |
| ------ | ---- | ------------------------------------- |
| `days` | int  | Number of days call records are kept. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "days": 90
    }
}
```

## Update Call Record Retention Policy

This path changes how long call records are kept, from their next pruning.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/call-records/retention` |

### Request Body

| Field  | Type | Required | Description |
| ------ | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `days` | int  | Yes      | 1–3650.     |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "days": 30
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "days": 30
    }
}
```

# Diameter

Diameter peers are the HSSs, SLFs, PCRFs, DRAs, SMSCs, MMEs and SMSFs Ella IMS connects to. Routes set the realm the requests of each routed application go to.

## Get the Diameter Identity

This path returns the Diameter identity of the IMS, derived from the operator settings.

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter` |

### Response Fields

| Field   | Type   | Description              |
| ------- | ------ | ------------------------ |
| `host`  | string | Origin-Host of the IMS.  |
| `realm` | string | Origin-Realm of the IMS. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "host": "ims.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "realm": "ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"
    }
}
```

## List Diameter Peers

This path returns the list of Diameter peers, in the order they were created in.

| Method | Path                     |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers` |

### Response Fields

| Field                   | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                    | string | Peer identifier, a UUIDv7.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `host`                  | string | DiameterIdentity of the peer, which must match the Origin-Host of its capabilities exchange. Empty takes the Origin-Host the peer gives.                                               |
| `address`               | string | IPv4 or IPv6 address of the peer.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `port`                  | int    | Port of the peer.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `transport`             | string | `tcp` or `sctp`.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `applications`          | array  | Applications the peer serves: `cx` for an HSS or an SLF, and `sh` and `s6c` for its IP-SM-GW functions; `rx` for a PCRF or a DRA; `sgd` for an SMSC, an MME or an SMSF.                |
| `priority`              | int    | Requests try the peers serving their application by priority, lowest first, and share them between peers of the same priority. SMSCs of the same service centre are tried by priority. |
| `service_centres`       | array  | Service centre addresses of an SMSC, E.164 numbers without `+`. Absent if none.                                                                                                        |
| `status`                | object | Connection to the peer.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `status.state`          | string | `down`, `connecting`, `open`, `suspect`, `reopen` or `closing`. `down` until the IMS has tried the peer.                                                                               |
| `status.since`          | string | Time of the last state change (RFC 3339).                                                                                                                                              |
| `status.remote_address` | string | Remote address of the connection.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `status.host`           | string | Origin-Host the peer gave in its last capabilities exchange, else the configured host.                                                                                                 |
| `status.realm`          | string | Origin-Realm the peer gave in its last capabilities exchange.                                                                                                                          |
| `status.error`          | string | Why the last connection to the peer failed.                                                                                                                                            |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "01a1796b-90b3-74bc-b148-bdc28999206e",
                "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "address": "127.0.0.1",
                "port": 3869,
                "transport": "tcp",
                "applications": ["cx"],
                "priority": 10,
                "status": {
                    "state": "down",
                    "since": "2026-10-26T18:14:14.963Z",
                    "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                    "error": "tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:0->127.0.0.1:3869: connect: connection refused"
                }
            },
            {
                "id": "01a1796b-90bb-7a57-8972-269dab84d5af",
                "host": "",
                "address": "127.0.0.1",
                "port": 3870,
                "transport": "tcp",
                "applications": ["rx"],
                "priority": 10,
                "status": {
                    "state": "down",
                    "since": "2026-10-26T18:14:14.971Z",
                    "error": "tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:0->127.0.0.1:3870: connect: connection refused"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Get a Diameter Peer

This path returns the details of a specific Diameter peer.

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type   | Description      |
| ---- | ------ | ---------------- |
| `id` | string | Peer identifier. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                  |
| ----- | ---------------------------- |
| `404` | No peer has this identifier. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": "01a1796b-90b3-74bc-b148-bdc28999206e",
        "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "address": "127.0.0.1",
        "port": 3869,
        "transport": "tcp",
        "applications": ["cx"],
        "priority": 10,
        "status": {
            "state": "down",
            "since": "2026-10-26T18:14:14.963Z",
            "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
            "error": "tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:0->127.0.0.1:3869: connect: connection refused"
        }
    }
}
```

## Create a Diameter Peer

This path creates a Diameter peer, which the IMS then connects to.

| Method | Path                     |
| ------ | ------------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/diameter/peers` |

### Request Body

| Field             | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`            | string | No       | Domain name. Unique among peers.                                                                        |
| `address`         | string | Yes      | Specific IPv4 or IPv6 address.                                                                          |
| `port`            | int    | No       | 1–65535. Default `3868`.                                                                                |
| `transport`       | string | No       | `tcp` or `sctp`. Default `tcp`.                                                                         |
| `applications`    | array  | Yes      | At least one of `cx`, `rx`, `sh`, `s6c` and `sgd`, each once.                                           |
| `priority`        | int    | No       | 0–65535. Default `10`.                                                                                  |
| `service_centres` | array  | No       | E.164 numbers of 1 to 15 digits, without `+`, each once. Requires `sgd` in `applications` and a `host`. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                       |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `409` | Another peer has the same host, or the same address and transport without a host. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
    "address": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 3869,
    "transport": "tcp",
    "applications": ["cx"],
    "priority": 10
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": "01a1796b-90b3-74bc-b148-bdc28999206e",
        "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "address": "127.0.0.1",
        "port": 3869,
        "transport": "tcp",
        "applications": ["cx"],
        "priority": 10,
        "status": {
            "state": "down"
        }
    }
}
```

## Update a Diameter Peer

This path replaces a Diameter peer, which the IMS then reconnects to. The request body is that of [Create a Diameter Peer](#create-a-diameter-peer).

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type   | Description      |
| ---- | ------ | ---------------- |
| `id` | string | Peer identifier. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                                      |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `404` | No peer has this identifier.                                                                                                                     |
| `409` | Another peer has the same host, or the same address and transport without a host; or the policy interface is `rx` and no other peer serves `rx`. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
    "address": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 3869,
    "transport": "tcp",
    "applications": ["cx"],
    "priority": 5
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": "01a1796b-90b3-74bc-b148-bdc28999206e",
        "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "address": "127.0.0.1",
        "port": 3869,
        "transport": "tcp",
        "applications": ["cx"],
        "priority": 5,
        "status": {
            "state": "down",
            "since": "2026-10-26T18:14:14.963Z",
            "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
            "error": "tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:0->127.0.0.1:3869: connect: connection refused"
        }
    }
}
```

## Delete a Diameter Peer

This path deletes a Diameter peer.

| Method | Path                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type   | Description      |
| ---- | ------ | ---------------- |
| `id` | string | Peer identifier. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                 |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `404` | No peer has this identifier.                                |
| `409` | The policy interface is `rx` and no other peer serves `rx`. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Diameter peer deleted"
    }
}
```

## List Diameter Routes

This path returns the route of each routed application: `cx`, `rx`, `sh`, then `s6c`.

| Method | Path                      |
| ------ | ------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/diameter/routes` |

### Response Fields

| Field               | Type   | Description                                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `application`       | string | `cx`, `rx`, `sh` or `s6c`.                                                                                            |
| `realm`             | string | Configured realm: of the HSS for `cx`, `sh` and `s6c`, of the PCRF for `rx`. Empty if not set.                        |
| `destination_realm` | string | Destination-Realm of the requests. If `realm` is empty: the `cx` realm for `sh` and `s6c`, the home domain otherwise. |
| `peers`             | array  | Peers serving the application, in the order requests try them, each with its `id`, `host`, `priority` and `status`.   |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "application": "cx",
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "destination_realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "peers": [
                    {
                        "id": "01a1796b-90b3-74bc-b148-bdc28999206e",
                        "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                        "priority": 5,
                        "status": {
                            "state": "down",
                            "since": "2026-10-26T18:14:21.052Z",
                            "host": "hss.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                            "error": "tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:0->127.0.0.1:3869: connect: connection refused"
                        }
                    }
                ]
            },
            {
                "application": "rx",
                "realm": "",
                "destination_realm": "ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "peers": [
                    {
                        "id": "01a1796b-90bb-7a57-8972-269dab84d5af",
                        "host": "",
                        "priority": 10,
                        "status": {
                            "state": "down",
                            "since": "2026-10-26T18:14:14.971Z",
                            "error": "tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:0->127.0.0.1:3870: connect: connection refused"
                        }
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Get a Diameter Route

This path returns the route of an application.

| Method | Path                                    |

### Path Parameters

### Response Codes

| ----- | ------------------------------ |
| `404` | The application is not routed. |

```
        "destination_realm": "ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",

            {
                "id": "01a1796b-90bb-7a57-8972-269dab84d5af",

                "priority": 10,

                    "state": "down",
                    "since": "2026-10-26T18:14:14.971Z",
                    "error": "tcp: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:0->127.0.0.1:3870: connect: connection refused"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Update a Diameter Route

This path sets the realm of an application's requests. The next request goes to the new realm.

### Path Parameters

| Name          | Type   | Description                |

### Request Body
